evidence.quote:
The design separates update proposals from resource management. An optimizer needs an identified target, a description of permitted edits, candidate evaluation, and a recorded activation decision. RSPL represents the target and retained versions; SEPL organizes those operations into an update loop. This separation permits common bookkeeping across resource types, while useful recovery additionally depends on which state is captured, which consumers bind to a version, and whether external effects occur.

G.2.4
Infrastructure Services

RSPL further includes cross-cutting services that support resource access, serialization, traceability, and retained-version recovery:

Model manager.
Routes calls by an explicit model name or configured role, with retry handling, a configured fallback, and usage logging.

Version manager.
Tracks resource version identifiers and lineage metadata. Recovery additionally requires retained configurations and implementation artifacts in the relevant resource manager or artifact store. A version string alone does not ensure an immutable snapshot or a failure-atomic update; these properties depend on the storage and activation implementation.

Dynamic manager.
Loads implementation classes from source strings or files into Python modules and supports schema/argument conversion. Resource managers use these facilities when constructing objects from records. Loading a new class does not by itself migrate existing instance state or rebind every consumer; activation and persistence remain separate management responsibilities.

Trace manager.
Records execution observations and links them to update decisions. Raw traces are not used for training or dataset synthesis by default; deployments must decide which fields to capture, redact, retain, and delete.

Recovery consistency requirements.

A complete restoration must realign the active configuration, the version metadata, and subsequent consumer resolution; restoring only one does not establish a consistent recovered state. Similarly, an interrupted update must not expose a candidate merely because its configuration was assigned before version registration completed. Version identities must preserve their associated retained content if they are to serve as restoration targets.

evidence.quote:
We additionally compare GPT-4o under at most three primary generation/refinement opportunities. Vanilla uses one unrefined answer; Self-Consistency (SC) samples three answers and votes; Best-of-3 (Bo3) uses a model judge; Simple Reflection (SR) produces an initial solution and two refinements without persistent resource updates; PS-Joint-Evo (Joint) edits the prompt and solution. All use the same reported route and decoding configuration, with a 32,768 output-token ceiling per call. This ceiling is not an equal realized-compute budget. Auxiliary reflection, editing, and evaluation calls must be distinguished from primary opportunities when interpreting the measured accuracy–cost trade-off.

Figure 3:
GPT-4o accuracy and cost (three runs). Boxes show the IQR and median; whiskers show the range. Bars show output tokens per problem (k). Appendix
B
gives exact results and settings.

Across three evaluations, joint editing reaches 59.09% mean accuracy on GPQA-Diamond versus 54.04% for Simple Reflection (351/594 versus 321/594 correct responses). On AIME24, it yields 15/90 versus 13/90 for Best-of-3; on AIME25, 12/90 versus 9/90 for Simple Reflection. Gains are 5.05, 2.22, and 3.33 percentage points, with approximately 61%, 57%, and 52% more output tokens than these respective controls. Denominators count repeated responses to the same 198 or 30 questions, not additional independent problems. These results characterize a higher-accuracy operating point at increased output-token cost, not an equal-compute advantage.

evidence.quote: Agent-Evo increases reported GAIA validation accuracy from 89.70 to 93.33 and test accuracy from 79.07 to 89.04 within the AGS configuration, and AGS scores 59.6 on HLE. Level 3 shows the largest test increase, from 61.22 to 81.63, but no validation increase, indicating that improvements differ across splits and difficulty levels. The within-AGS comparisons share the reported backbone and planner–specialist organization. External leaderboard entries contextualize these scores, but differences in backbones, tools, and inference budgets prevent a controlled comparison.

evidence.quote:
The Memory case changes retention and retrieval after compaction. On the same 45-record workload, returned constraints increase from zero to eight, with 25 ordinary recent records preserved. Because the updated policy also adds storage, this is a retrieval result rather than a task-accuracy gain. Across the three cases, different failure signals lead to resource-specific edits under the same sequence of candidate checks, commit, and subsequent invocation. The edited object determines the check: spreadsheet processing checks returned data, the Environment case checks transition behavior, and the Memory case checks retrieved records. Each check concerns the edited resource’s behavior; an accepted version becomes available for subsequent task execution through its registered interface.

6
Limitations and Impact Statement

Empirical scope.
The quantitative evaluations assess configured AGS pipelines, including the work required to propose and evaluate edits. GPT-4o controls primary generation opportunities rather than total computation; each AIME set has only 30 questions. The cases illustrate selected accepted updates, not population-level gains. We do not isolate resource management from the update strategy or establish equal-cost superiority, cross-task transfer, or recovery after faulty activation. Conclusions concern the interface and its evaluated uses, not general deployment reliability.

evidence.quote:
Prompt resources expose names, versions, evolvability flags, templates, and rendering variables; the prompt server delegates lifecycle operations to its context manager. The version manager stores version metadata, while retained prompt configurations reside in the prompt context manager. Unregister removes the active prompt binding but retains its local history; cleanup clears that manager’s configurations and history. Restoration acts on retained prompt state and is not a system-wide transaction.

Datasets.

The reasoning benchmarks contain 198 GPQA-Diamond questions, 30 AIME24 problems, and 30 AIME25 problems (released in two 15-problem parts). The GPQA-Diamond loader shuffles answer options with a fixed preprocessing seed of 42; this is not an LLM decoding seed.

Resource identities, accepted versions, and trace-linked decisions.

AGP specifies a common resource-update interface, whereas the cited optimizers define proposal or search procedures and the state needed to support them. The distinction is not absolute: for example, GEPA records candidate ancestry and AFlow records parent edits, while Alita explicitly stores generated tools for reuse. An AGP adapter would need to map such state to resource identities, candidate evaluation, and activation decisions; a shared interface alone does not verify that mapping. Our main experiments use reflection, and the alternative adapters remain unevaluated sketches.

AGP’s management contract requires rejection to preserve the active binding, while restoration targets a retained internal version. The cases document accepted updates, not recovery after a bad version becomes active. The reported target ablations compare what is revised within AGS; they do not isolate resource management while holding the editor, feedback, and realized budget fixed. Persistent storage alone likewise does not establish transfer to unseen tasks.

evidence.quote:
Each collected record is normalized into a task specification, official examples, a language-specific starter template, and difficulty and topic metadata. The preprocessing preserves judge-required signatures and class definitions, filters malformed and duplicate records, and checks template availability for the target languages. We select 100 recently released problems from the collected pool and instantiate them across all five languages. This selection aims to reduce contamination risk, but release recency alone cannot establish whether a task was absent from a model’s training data.

Problem Characteristics.

Each task specifies input and output behavior, constraints, and a required submission interface. The selected categories span different algorithmic and data-structure requirements, while hidden tests can expose boundary cases and implementation errors. The common task specifications support comparisons across languages; they do not eliminate language-specific compiler or runtime effects.

Problem Evaluation.

For each problem, the agent receives the task representation and submits code to the platform judge, which checks hidden tests and reports the available execution statistics. The reported Solution-Evo budget permits at most three submissions: the initial solution and up to two feedback-driven revisions, with the task specification and submission interface held fixed. Vanilla uses the initial solution without these revisions. This comparison measures the combined effect of feedback-driven revision and additional attempts, rather than an equal-computation advantage.
evidence.support_explanation: 100题五语言；最多三次提交与一次Vanilla是额外尝试效果。

evidence.quote:
We report three groups of metrics that capture complementary aspects of code-agent performance. Capability metrics evaluate functional correctness and diagnose execution-blocking failure modes. PR measures the number of fully accepted problems, while TLE, MLE, CE, RE, WA, TO, and RpE identify whether failures arise from algorithmic inefficiency, excessive memory use, compilation errors, runtime exceptions, incorrect logic, response timeout, or invalid output formatting. These metrics are particularly important for self-evolving agents because different failure modes correspond to different refinement opportunities.

AR and AM summarize runtime and memory over each method’s accepted solutions. Because those sets can differ, these aggregates do not isolate per-problem efficiency; a common-solved-set paired analysis is required. APC measures passed-test coverage rather than resource efficiency, with larger values denoting more passed cases in the reported aggregate. Its interpretation also depends on which submissions contribute and how many tests each task contains.

Platform-relative metrics aggregate the reported runtime and memory percentiles of accepted submissions. These percentiles describe a changing submission distribution rather than a controlled human baseline. Their interpretation depends on the accepted set and aggregation procedure.
